subject.title: fix(plugins): detect orphan diagnostics with explicit code marker (2-part fix)

question: Should the legacy no-code stale diagnostic cleanup stay in runtime snapshot loading, or should that shipped-row cleanup move to doctor/migration-owned repair before merge?
rationale: The PR follows the predecessor's explicit-marker direction for new diagnostics, but the legacy runtime fallback is a compatibility-sensitive persisted-state behavior choice that tests alone should not silently decide.

options.title: Require legacy proof, then accept runtime fallback
options.body: Keep the PR open until redacted latest-head output or logs show a pre-code SQLite diagnostics_json row rederives and Gateway startup proceeds, then land if exact-head checks pass.

options.title: Accept source and test proof
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally override the remaining proof gap and accept the runtime fallback based on source inspection and regression tests.

options.title: Move legacy cleanup out of runtime
options.body: Ask the author to drop the no-code runtime fallback and handle shipped persisted rows through doctor or migration-owned cleanup instead.

recommendation.title: Require legacy proof, then accept runtime fallback
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open until redacted latest-head output or logs show a pre-code SQLite diagnostics_json row rederives and Gateway startup proceeds, then land if exact-head checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: Most directly connected to the merged persisted diagnostic stale-source history and current-main ownership signal for these files.
